title: Treasury Laws Amendment (North Queensland Flood Recovery) Bill 2019
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (North Queensland Flood Recovery) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change the tax treatment of specified Queensland disaster assistance and fund loans supporting primary producers affected by the 2019 North Queensland floods.
It would exclude qualifying flood grants from taxable income, exempt specified storm assistance payments and appropriate $1.75 billion for loans through participating financial institutions.
Tax measures would apply from the 2018-19 income year, while the loan appropriation would commence the day after royal assent to support eligible flood-affected producers.
changes: Category C and D grants for floods starting between 25 January and 28 February 2019 would receive non-assessable, non-exempt treatment.
Qualifying farm infrastructure, restocking and replanting grants would receive the same tax treatment.
Covered Fassifern Valley assistance for the October 2018 storm would be exempt income, but could affect tax losses.
The loan scheme would provide participating financial institutions with low-interest funding for up to three years.
summary.affected: Eligible flood-affected small businesses, primary producers and non-profit organisations, covered storm-affected producers, and participating financial institutions are affected.

speeches.speaker: Cathy O'Toole
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (North Queensland Flood Recovery) Bill 2019 but condemned the LNP government's disaster recovery criteria, citing cases like Cherrie Vitalli denied three times and small business owner Warren Figg waiting six weeks for a grant, and noting that only $724,112 of $27.2 million in relief had been delivered to Townsville businesses.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The bill makes qualifying disaster payments, recovery grants, and on-farm grants to flood-affected Queensland primary producers, small businesses, and non-profit organisations non-assessable for tax; treats storm-damage payments to Fassifern Valley primary producers as exempt income; and provides a special appropriation for a reduced‑interest loan scheme for eligible primary producers.
